references.text: Hobab, Moses' father-in-law (or brother-in-law), is asked to join the Israelites, but he says he will return to his own land and his people, mirroring Jethro's departure to his own land.
Hobab expresses his wish to return to his land and his people, a parallel to Jethro's journey home described in Exodus 18:27.
Moses took leave of his father-in-law Jethro when he returned to Egypt, and here we see the reverse situation where Jethro takes leave of Moses.
Jethro came from Midian to meet Moses, and this verse concludes his visit with him returning to his land.
Jethro is introduced as a priest in Midian, and the land he returns to in 18:27 is precisely Midian.
The verses capture the beginning (meeting) and end (farewell) of Jethro's visit, showing continuity in their respectful relationship throughout the events.
A clear contrast: In Judges 19:7, the father-in-law uses force to keep a guest against his will, while in Exodus 18:27, Jethro shows respect for God's call by willingly letting Moses go.
